messages:
mia.nguyen: Heads-up — planning to provision a new GPU nodepool in ap-southeast3 for burst inference (customer trial). Need preemptible fallback strategy, quotas look tight.
raj.patel: +1. What's our primary SKU target? A10G or A2/H100? Cost vs latency tradeoff.
sophie.kim: For trial we were thinking A10G (good mm/perf) with preemptible A100/T4 fallback? but A100 quotas are limited in that region.
alex.morris: If A10G is primary, fallback to T4 is cheaper but will hurt throughput. Also T4 requires different device plugin tuning — will that break our autoscaler scaling heuristics?
leo.huang: cluster-autoscaler only cares about pods pending due to insufficient resources. mixing GPU SKUs is fine but we need proper nodeSelector/affinity + taints so heavy models go to A10G.
amanda.davies: Two operational asks: 1) ensure autoscaler respects GPU count per node label for scheduling; 2) prevent scale-down of nodes with local PVs used by model caches.
mia.nguyen: Agreed. Proposed plan: create pool-a10g (3x A10G preemptible nodes initially), pool-fallback-t4 (preemptible), and pool-oncall-a10g (non-preemptible reserved for low-latency customers). Use taints: gpu-primary=true:NoSchedule on pool-a10g and gpu-fallback=true:NoSchedule on pool-fallback-t4. Pods set tolerations+preferredAffinity.
raj.patel: That works. What about quota requests to cloud? ap-southeast3 GPU quota is low — I've started a ticket with cloud-support (case 987654). infra-bot: quota-request-submitted: case=987654 region=ap-southeast3 resource=GPUs details=+8-A10G, +12-T4
sophie.kim: We also need a scale-up priority policy: when pending pods request a10g GPUs, prefer pool-a10g; if pool-a10g unable due to quota, then create nodes in fallback pool and set image/tooling to degrade gracefully.
alex.morris: Can we use nodePoolSelector in CA? CA handles different pools; but we can set different max nodes per pool. Also set expander to "least-waste" to minimize overprovisioning.
leo.huang: FYI — NAT egress IPs in that region are limited. Adding new nodepools may increase egress SNAT mappings. Anyone using static egress IPs for customers?
amanda.davies: yes one customer pins their IPs. We need to ensure new pools use the same NAT gateway/subnet or reserve additional NAT capacity. Otherwise we'll hit ephemeral ip exhaustion.
mia.nguyen: Good catch. I'll coordinate with networking to reserve extra NAT ports and ensure new pools use the private subnet. Also we'll add nodePool annotation to opt into the customer-egress route.
raj.patel: What about preemptions — do we want to use GCP preemptible or provider spot? Need graceful eviction handling. Our agent must checkpoint KV cache before eviction.
sophie.kim: Add a PodDisruptionBudget and implement a PreemptionHandler sidecar for model-server pods that will attempt to flush caches to object storage on SIGTERM. For critical pods set podPriority > default.
alex.morris: Example nodepool create snippet (GKE):
```
gcloud container node-pools create pool-a10g \
  --cluster=redwood-prod-apse3 \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-16 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a10g,count=1 \
  --preemptible \
  --num-nodes=3 \
  --node-labels=gpu-type=a10g,pool=primary \
  --taints=gpu-primary=true:NoSchedule
```
leo.huang: Also add autoscaling settings:
```
gcloud container node-pools update pool-a10g --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=1 --max-nodes=12
```
amanda.davies: Drain behavior note: we had a failure last week where drain got stuck because of local model cache PVs. Log excerpt:
```
ERROR: node drain failed: pod model-cache-xyz uses local-volume; eviction blocked
```
mia.nguyen: To avoid that, we'll set those caches on shared PVC backed by regional disks or S3, not local. For tiny warm caches we can tolerate eviction but for larger ones move to shared store.
raj.patel: Timeline? Need to tell trial team.
mia.nguyen: I'll open infra-change PR today with pool configs, network request, and autoscaler settings. If cloud support approves quota by EOD tomorrow we can provision Thursday.
sophie.kim: I'll add CI smoke tests to validate GPU plugin on fallback pool and check scheduling across pools.
alex.morris: If quota is delayed, backup: spin up fewer reserved non-preemptible A10G nodes for the pilot and cap user concurrency.
leo.huang: tagging infra-owners: @sophie.kim @mia.nguyen for follow-ups.
infra-bot: deploy-note: infra-change-pr opened #1234 by mia.nguyen
amanda.davies: sounds good. please include runbook steps for manual failover from A10G to fallback T4 (commands + am IOPS check).
mia.nguyen: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
